issue_context.title: networkd sometimes crashes on restart with "assertion failed"
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > systemd 247 (247.2-1~bpo10+1)

**Used distribution**
 > Debian Buster

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
 > 4.19.0-13-amd64 #1 SMP Debian 4.19.160-2 (2020-11-28) x86_64 GNU/Linux

**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
 > amd64

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > systemd-networkd sometimes crashes when restarting, with the error message
 "Assertion 'a' failed at src/network/networkd-address.c:1857, function address_is_ready(). Aborting."
 This seems to be somewhat random and is only triggered by sufficiently "complex" configuration.

**Steps to reproduce the problem**

Contents of `/etc/systemd/network`:
  * `test.netdev`:

        [NetDev]
        Name = test
        Kind = dummy

  * `test2.netdev`:

        [NetDev]
        Name = test2
        Kind = dummy

  * `test.network`:

        [Match]
        Name = test

        [Network]
        Address = 10.0.0.1/32

        [RoutingPolicyRule]
        Family = both
        IncomingInterface = test
        Table = 42
        Priority = 42

        [Route]
        Table = 42
        Destination = 10.0.0.0/24
        Gateway = 0.0.0.0

  * `test2.network`:

        [Match]
        Name = test2

        [Network]
        Address = 10.1.0.1/32

        [RoutingPolicyRule]
        Family = both
        IncomingInterface = test2
        Table = 42
        Priority = 42

        [Route]
        Table = 42
        Destination = 10.1.0.0/24
        Gateway = 0.0.0.0

  * `99-dhcp.network`:

        [Match]
        Name=e*

        [Network]
        DHCP=yes

Now run `systemctl restart systemd-networkd`. The crash does not always happen,
so you might need to restart it a few times. The above configuration is a
"minimum" that reliably triggered the crash in my tests.

It looks like networkd crashes before it can fully apply the routes that it gets
through DHCP because after the crash the default route is missing:
```
root@fednet-debug:~# ip r
default via 172.21.127.1 dev ens6 proto dhcp src 172.21.127.222 metric 1024
172.21.127.0/24 dev ens6 proto kernel scope link src 172.21.127.222
172.21.127.1 dev ens6 proto dhcp scope link src 172.21.127.222 metric 1024
root@fednet-debug:~# systemctl restart systemd-networkd   # Now networkd crashes (and systemd gives up trying to restart it)
root@fednet-debug:~# ip r
172.21.127.0/24 dev ens6 proto kernel scope link src 172.21.127.222
```

comments: Hmm... I found the root of this issue. But it is slightly hard to fix... Anyway, thank you for the report.

Based on internal discussion, let's reassign to the next milestone.
The issue is unpleasant, but the crash only happens on  restart, and `systemd-networkd.service` has `Restart=true`, so it'll get reexecuted and the effect of the crash is limited. We don't have a fix for this yet, and we don't know how involved the patch will be, so let's drop it from the milestone for now.

Are there any suggested workarounds for this?  I'm seeing the same crash on 247.3-3ubuntu3 (Ubuntu 21.04), and it crashes so rapidly and reliably that systemd gives up on it with `Start request repeated too quickly`.  Thus the effect of the crash is not "limited" for me; the machine never gets a default route and has no Internet access.

Happy to try patches, etc.
Now I am working on this. #19445 is the WIP PR.

> Are there any suggested workarounds for this? I'm seeing the same crash on 247.3-3ubuntu3 (Ubuntu 21.04), and it crashes so rapidly and reliably that systemd gives up on it with `Start request repeated too quickly`. Thus the effect of the crash is not "limited" for me; the machine never gets a default route and has no Internet access.
> 
> Happy to try patches, etc.


I have managed to sort it on my environment by running 
```
ip link set eth1 down 
systemctl reset-failed systemd-networkd 
systemctl restart systemd-networkd
```
`eth1` is an interface that has `RoutingPolicyRule` and extra routes on additional route table

Adding `KeepConfiguration=dhcp` to the DHCP-enabled interface is a workaround that worked for me in some cases. Weirdly, `KeepConfiguration=dhcp-on-stop` was not enough in those cases.

Furthermore, I ran into a case where adding the global config property `ManageForeignRoutes=False` triggered this issue. In this case, it again affected only hosts with a DHCP-enabled (uplink) interface, even though they already have `KeepConfiguration=dhcp`. Any idea why this occurs when adding `ManageForeignRoutes=False` and how to work around it?
